note: Members ponatinib (approved 2012 on PACE), flumatinib (China, first line vs imatinib) and vamotinib (phase 1); Ba/F3 and mouse BCR-ABL models and a mutagenesis screen predicted activity, exposure and mutation coverage.
label: CML (ABL1 inhibitors)

engagement.model: BCR-ABL cell lines and mouse leukemia/xenograft models
engagement.quote: AP24534 inhibited all tested BCR-ABL mutants in cellular and biochemical assays, suppressed BCR-ABL(T315I)-driven tumor growth in mice, and completely abrogated resistance in cell-based mutagenesis screens.
engagement.note: Ponatinib (AP24534) blocked BCR-ABL signalling, including T315I, in Ba/F3 cells and suppressed T315I tumours in mice.
engagement.short: Pan-BCR-ABL inhibition in cells and mice
engagement.judgement: Opening entry: the system first used for this class; the PD readout (BCR-ABL/CRKL phosphorylation) has a direct patient counterpart.

engagement.magnitude_basis: share of patients with >=50% pCRKL reduction against BCR-ABL inhibition in Ba/F3 cells
engagement.confidence_note: Patient side from the PMC author manuscript full text; model side abstract-level (CRKL readout in the mouse/cell work not confirmed in full text).
engagement.model: BCR-ABL cell lines and mouse leukemia/xenograft models
engagement.quote: At doses of 15 mg or more, 32 of 34 patients (94%) had a reduction of 50% or more in CRKL phosphorylation, including 8 of 10 patients (80%) with the T315I mutation
engagement.note: pCRKL, the BCR-ABL substrate readout, fell >=50% in 94% of patients at >=15 mg, T315I included.
engagement.short: pCRKL suppressed in patients incl. T315I
engagement.judgement: Paired comparison: the phase 1 paper reports CRKL inhibition but does not set it beside the preclinical readout. Tiered proximal (direct substrate of the target kinase). NCT00660920 has no posted results.

dose.quote: AP24534 inhibited all tested BCR-ABL mutants in cellular and biochemical assays, suppressed BCR-ABL(T315I)-driven tumor growth in mice, and completely abrogated resistance in cell-based mutagenesis screens.
dose.note: Cell-based mutagenesis screens defined 40 nM ponatinib as the concentration that suppressed all resistant BCR-ABL clones.
dose.judgement: The screen stated a concentration target (40 nM) that a human trial could check; untested until patient PK.

dose.magnitude_basis: 45 mg steady-state trough (~64 nM) against the 40 nM screen threshold
dose.confidence_note: PMC author manuscript full text; FDA clinical pharmacology review gives 45 mg steady-state Cmin 34 ng/mL (about 64 nM).
dose.quote: At doses of 30 mg or more, trough blood concentrations surpassed the 40 nM concentration that was found to completely suppress the emergence of BCR-ABL mutations in preclinical studies
dose.note: Troughs exceeded the 40 nM screen threshold at >=30 mg; 45 mg was taken forward.
dose.judgement: Scored same: the target was reached. The screen stated no tolerability margin, so margin_stated is null; arterial occlusive events at 45 mg and OPTIC's later response-based reduction to 15 mg (below the 40 nM trough) are safety and efficacy matters, not a dose miss under the brief.

efficacy.model: BCR-ABL cell lines and mouse leukemia/xenograft models
efficacy.quote: AP24534 inhibited all tested BCR-ABL mutants in cellular and biochemical assays, suppressed BCR-ABL(T315I)-driven tumor growth in mice, and completely abrogated resistance in cell-based mutagenesis screens.
efficacy.note: T315I-driven leukemia and xenograft mice responded to ponatinib; benefit in TKI-resistant CML predicted.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry for the class track.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: MCyR rate in CP-CML against tumour regression/survival in T315I mice
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Europe PMC); single-arm trial, response against historical expectation.
efficacy.model: BCR-ABL cell lines and mouse leukemia/xenograft models
efficacy.quote: Among 267 patients with chronic-phase CML, 56% had a major cytogenetic response (51% of patients with resistance to or unacceptable side effects from dasatinib or nilotinib and 70% of patients with the T315I mutation)

patient_trials.quote: Of 12 patients who had chronic-phase CML with the T315I mutation, 100% had a complete hematologic response and 92% had a major cytogenetic response.

efficacy.note: PACE primary endpoint met: 56% MCyR in chronic phase, 70% in T315I, as the T315I mice predicted.
efficacy.judgement: Paired: PACE does not cite the mouse data side by side. Phase 1 (primary endpoint MTD) kept as a patient_trials record.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: MMR at 6 months vs imatinib against preclinical superiority over imatinib
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level for both; model side known only from the Leukemia 2010 letter title (no abstract), so the exact cell lines and mouse models are not confirmed.
efficacy.model: BCR-ABL cell lines and mouse leukemia/xenograft models
efficacy.quote: The rate of major molecular response (MMR) at 6 months (primary endpoint) was significantly higher with flumatinib than with imatinib (33.7% vs. 18.3%; P = 0.0006)

patient_trials.quote: The MTD was 600 mg with the Grade-3 psoriasis-like skin toxicity as the DLT.

efficacy.note: Flumatinib, preclinically more potent than imatinib, beat imatinib on 6-month MMR in first-line CML (NCT02204644).
efficacy.judgement: Same model family (BCR-ABL cell lines and mice), so the flumatinib program shares the track; the 2010 claim 'outperforms imatinib' is the prediction tested. Vamotinib's phase 1 (Turkina 2025; primary endpoint MTD, 5 of 16 T315I responders against mouse survival 'similar to ponatinib') is recorded under patient_trials and scores no status. NCT02204644 has no posted results.

efficacy.quote: AP24534 inhibited all tested BCR-ABL mutants in cellular and biochemical assays, suppressed BCR-ABL(T315I)-driven tumor growth in mice, and completely abrogated resistance in cell-based mutagenesis screens.
efficacy.note: Mutagenesis screen predicted no single BCR-ABL mutation would escape ponatinib at clinical concentrations.
efficacy.short: No single mutant escapes at 40 nM
efficacy.judgement: Patient-level prediction: which mutation carriers respond.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: single-mutation resistance in patients against the screen
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Europe PMC). Compound mutations, which the screens also flagged, were not checked here.
efficacy.quote: No single BCR-ABL mutation conferring resistance to ponatinib was detected.
efficacy.note: Responses occurred regardless of baseline mutation; no single resistance mutation emerged, as the screen predicted.
efficacy.short: No single resistant mutation in PACE
efficacy.judgement: Paired comparison; the abstract states responses 'regardless of the baseline BCR-ABL kinase domain mutation status'. Scored on the mutation-level prediction, not on the primary MCyR rate.

efficacy.confidence_note: model_kind ex_vivo because the enum has no in-vitro cell-line value; engineered murine cell line.
efficacy.model: Ba/F3 cells engineered with clinically reported BCR-ABL1 compound mutants (in vitro IC50 profiling)
efficacy.note: Ba/F3 panel of clinically reported compound mutants profiled ponatinib IC50s; T315I-inclusive compounds predicted high-level ponatinib resistance.
efficacy.quote: T315I-inclusive compound mutants confer high-level resistance to TKIs, including ponatinib.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry at the panel's first use; comparison with patients is in the same paper.
efficacy.population: Ph+ CML and ALL patients treated with ponatinib, compound mutation carriers

efficacy.magnitude_basis: ponatinib IC50 vs mean plasma level at 45 mg; response or failure per patient
efficacy.confidence_note: Patient series is small (handful of ponatinib failures plus three durable responders); mixes CML and Ph+ ALL. Full text read via PMC4160372.
efficacy.model: Ba/F3 cells engineered with clinically reported BCR-ABL1 compound mutants (in vitro IC50 profiling)
efficacy.note: Patients with T315I-inclusive compound mutants (E255V/T315I, Y253H/T315I, T315I/H396R) failed ponatinib; non-T315I compound carriers responded durably, as IC50s ranked.
efficacy.short: IC50 ranking matched ponatinib failures, retrodiction
efficacy.quote: In vitro resistance profiling was predictive of treatment outcomes in Ph(+) leukemia patients.
efficacy.judgement: Retrodiction: the mutants were chosen because they were already clinically reported and the patient outcomes were known when the IC50s were run, so retro, not same.
efficacy.population: Ph+ CML and ALL patients treated with ponatinib, compound mutation carriers

efficacy.magnitude_basis: ponatinib resistance in patients by BCR-ABL1 genotype against the screen's recovered resistant clones
efficacy.population: BCR::ABL1-positive (Ph+) CML and Ph+ ALL treated with ponatinib, compound mutation carriers
efficacy.confidence_note: PMC4160372 full text read. Patients pooled from ponatinib trials with CML and Ph+ ALL; registry_date null because the paper's patient series is not one registered trial's results record.
efficacy.note: T315I-inclusive compound mutants (E255V/T315I) caused clinical ponatinib failure; the 2009 screen had recovered that mutant, though its headline claimed complete abrogation of resistance.
efficacy.short: Compound mutants escape ponatinib, as screen flagged
efficacy.quote: Vulnerability of ponatinib to certain two-component compound mutations was demonstrated in pre-clinical studies (O'Hare et al., 2009), suggesting they may emerge as a clinical problem in patients treated with ponatinib.
efficacy.reason: Screen-flagged compound mutants escaped in patients
efficacy.judgement: Scored same with source_calls_it partial, not contra: the source states the 2009 screen recovered E255V/T315I and flagged compound mutants, and patients failed with them; the abstract's 'completely abrogated resistance' overstated coverage at clinical exposure. Strengthens the 2013 same: the source states the comparison itself and extends it to compound mutants.

safety.magnitude_basis: organ systems flagged in rat/monkey (heart, liver, pancreas) against patient serious safety concerns
safety.confidence_note: FDA review in the source bundle; the reviewers call the animal cardiac findings low-incidence and non-dose-dependent.
safety.model: Rat and cynomolgus monkey repeat-dose toxicology
safety.quote: These findings combined and evidence of a possible dose-dependent effect on necrosis of myocardial cells in the 6-month monkey toxicology study may be relevant to the clinically observed cardiovascular toxicities observed.
safety.note: Monkey heart murmurs and myocardial necrosis, ALT/AST rises and pancreatic necrosis matched patient cardiovascular, hepatic and pancreatic toxicity; arterial thrombosis itself was not modelled.
safety.judgement: Judgement call: same with source_calls_it partial rather than contra. The review links the animal cardiac findings to clinical cardiovascular toxicity and the liver and pancreas findings map to boxed hepatotoxicity and DLT pancreatitis, but no animal showed arterial occlusion, the boxed harm. Monkeys could in principle show vascular occlusion, so a stricter reading would add a contra for arterial thrombosis (PACE 2013, label 2012).

safety.model: Human iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes, endothelial cells and cardiac fibroblasts (in vitro TKI toxicity screen)
safety.note: hiPSC cardiomyocytes, endothelial cells and fibroblasts screened approved TKIs; ponatinib among the most cytotoxic, producing a cardiac safety index.
safety.short: hiPSC screen ranks ponatinib highly cardiotoxic
safety.quote: Sorafenib, regorafenib, and ponatinib were highly cytotoxic in all eleven healthy control hiPSC-CM lines, demonstrated via quantitative and qualitative viability assays.
safety.judgement: Opening entry at first use; the screen ran four years after ponatinib's arterial occlusive events were public.
safety.population: Patients on ponatinib (CML and Ph+ ALL)

safety.magnitude_basis: hiPSC LD50 ranking vs clinical cardiovascular adverse events
safety.confidence_note: Full text read via PMC5409837. Patient side is cited clinical experience, not a trial dataset; cytotoxic concentrations exceed clinical plasma levels (authors note).
safety.model: Human iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes, endothelial cells and cardiac fibroblasts (in vitro TKI toxicity screen)
safety.note: High hiPSC endothelial toxicity for ponatinib matched the vascular toxicity already seen in patients; cytotoxicity occurred only at micromolar concentrations.
safety.short: Endothelial toxicity matches known vascular harm
safety.quote: The high hiPSC-EC toxicity we observed with VEGFR2/PDGFR-inhibiting TKIs such as ponatinib corroborates with vascular toxicity observed clinically with these TKIs
safety.judgement: Retrodiction run after the 2013 PACE and EPIC vascular events, so retro; ponatinib's own cell death needed micromolar concentrations, far above clinical exposure, so partial.
safety.population: Patients on ponatinib (CML and Ph+ ALL)

safety.model: Biochemical kinase-selectivity profiling (VEGFR2 and other off-target kinases spared vs ponatinib)
safety.note: Vamotinib (PF-114) designed for narrower kinase selectivity than ponatinib, predicting avoidance of ponatinib's cardiovascular toxicity.
safety.quote: PF-114 is a novel TKI developed with the specifications of (i) targeting T315I and other resistance mutations in BCR/ABL; (ii) achieving a high selectivity to improve safety
safety.judgement: Opening entry at the model's first public use (epub November 2014).
safety.population: CML failing second-generation TKI or with T315I

safety.confidence_note: Full text PMC12141164. NCT02885766 has no posted results (checked 2026-11-07), so registry_date null. Model side (Mian 2015) read at abstract level; the profiling itself is in its ref 26.
safety.model: Biochemical kinase-selectivity profiling (VEGFR2 and other off-target kinases spared vs ponatinib)
safety.note: Phase 1 (n=51, median 6 months) saw no vascular occlusive events or ankle-brachial index changes; authors tie this to vamotinib sparing VEGFR2 and related kinases.
safety.short: No vascular occlusion in vamotinib phase 1
safety.quote: Comparison of kinase inhibition profiles of ponatinib and vamotinib [ 26 ] may suggest that inhibition of EPHA6, EPHA7, TAK1, TIE2, VEGFR2, ZAK kinases by ponatinib but not vamotinib may contribute to cardiovascular toxicity of the former.
safety.reason: No vascular events in small phase 1
safety.judgement: Source sets the kinase profile beside the absent vascular events, so comparison_stated true; small, short phase 1 cannot exclude late arterial events, so low confidence and partial.
safety.population: CML failing >=1 second-generation TKI or with T315I (NCT02885766)
